outcome.description: She thanks you with the kind of voice that hasn't said thank you in a while. The skiff peels off, slower than it came in.
She listens, asks twice if you're sure, and then thanks you anyway. The skiff turns onto the heading you gave her.
She doesn't believe the relief station exists. Says you're trying to send her to nothing. Says she'll take what she came for.
Her voice gets very flat. The skiff opens up.
He holds the line for a long beat. Then mutters about sloppy intel and breaks off.
He doesn't buy it for a second. Says the sources are paid well for a reason. The rustrunner's guns swing into line.
He does the math on his face. Then peels off without another word.
He laughs. Says his bosses scare him more than yours. Weapons hot.
He doesn't talk either. The rustrunner accelerates.
He chews on that. Then he tells the other picket to stand down. Says the contract holds.
He says the contract's the problem, not the answer. He waves his wingman back and closes in alone.
He looks at his wingman. He looks at you. He says they have other contracts to break.
He figures one picket is enough for you. His wingman holds station while he opens the engagement.
He thanks you twice and then a third time. The raider banks away fast, like the kid won't keep until he gets there.
He sends the clinic's fire report unasked. You give him what you can spare and he's gone. The cost is 60 credits in supplies.
He watches the pause run long. Decides you've already chosen.
He doesn't argue. He just opens fire.
